Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J28/J28nB219.xml). Recorded Sayings of Zhuanyu Guanheng: the record compiler labels the section for lineage-son Xiyi and immediately identifies Xiyi as Fasong; Zhuanyu Guanheng is the record-owner, not the utterer.

Source record (J/J29/J29nB239.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Chuiwan: Chuiwan Guangzhen says Mazu became a lineage son only after prolonged service and testing, using the title for recognized teacher-disciple succession.

Occurrences.Kwic: 慟惟新寂法子顯微元侍者
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J28/J28nB220.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Faxi Yin: In a funeral address Faxi Yin calls the deceased attendant Xianweiyuan his newly departed lineage son and recalls the transmission placed in his hands.

Senses.Explanation: A lineage son or heir is a person placed in Zhuanyu Guanheng’s transmitted family in the opening witness, not an ordinary child and not merely someone who studies nearby. Zhuanyu Guanheng’s record titles Xiyi as his lineage son; Chuiwan Guangzhen uses the title for Mazu after service and testing; Faxi Yin addresses the deceased Xianweiyuan as his lineage son while recalling a handed-down house style. The title does not by itself prove every historical lineage claim outside the stored passages.

Occurrences.Kwic: 要知省事法子，一切處看。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J34/J34nB301.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Nanyue Jiqi: Nanyue Jiqi Hongchu says that if one wants to know the means for simplifying matters, one should look in every circumstance.

Source record (J/J27/J27nB194.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Zhangxue Zui: Zhangxue Zui says earlier worthies exhausted hundreds of plans and every kind of means to make people take hold before a thought arises.

Occurrences.Kwic: 也得箇撐持家道底法子。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J29/J29nB239.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Chuiwan: Chuiwan Guangzhen criticizes learned gestures that may provide a means to prop up the house style but fail at death.

Senses.Explanation: A means is a way devised or relied on to accomplish something; in these Chan addresses the word names an instrument of action, not a disciple. Nanyue Jiqi Hongchu names a “means for simplifying matters.” Zhangxue Zui says earlier worthies exhausted every means, while Chuiwan Guangzhen calls a stock performance a means for propping up a house style and then attacks its limits. No stored occurrence makes a particular means universally valid; Chuiwan’s example is explicitly inadequate.
